findings:
The plan is mostly sound. It builds the Dreadnought on the parts, launch bays, phase ladder and hazard machinery that Phases 10 and 11 shipped, and does not rebuild any of it. Four design defects block it, though. The five-rocket missile fan has no place it can be configured before its rocket pools are sized, so rockets would be silently refused. One shared attack gate cuts a three-gun broadside down to one gun. The torpedo's "three hits to defuse" is in the wrong units, so any single player shot kills it. And the opening test-time task asks for 12 s back with no measured candidates, while every Dreadnought task waits on it. I would send it back for a re-plan that fixes these four and folds in the ten minor corrections below.

| # | Severity | Problem | Fix | Tasks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | blocking | The missile-fan rack's fan count, salvo and cooldown have no authoring path: turret slots can't override them, each variant has one shared scene, and pools are sized when the mount is built. | Add a new variant with its own standalone scene (as the heavy cannon has), or a slot override applied before the pools are sized. | t3, t8 |
| B2 | blocking | Every mount shares one zero-argument attack gate that can't tell which weapon is asking, so at the cap of 2 the middle and rear cannons of a side already firing are refused. | After building the mounts, give each one a gate bound to its own part, and add a row proving a full side volley fires while the missile rack is busy. | t8 |
| B3 | blocking | The torpedo's health of 3 counts damage, not hits, and the player's default shot deals 50, so one shot from any weapon defuses it. | Set its health in damage units taken from the shipped weapon modes, and test the defuse with real player bullets. | t4 |
| B4 | blocking | The first task must free at least 12 s of test time but names no file and no measurement, earlier phases report the easy speed-ups used up, and only about 2–6 s is actually needed. | List measured candidate files, set the target to the time actually needed with an escalation path, and allow (or rule out) behaviour-identical code speed-ups like Phase 8's. | t1, t6 |
| M1 | minor | The one-engine turn-radius test expects a ratio of about 2.9, but the plan's own numbers give about 10, and the side-choice rule can then pick an orbit the ship can no longer turn tightly enough to hold. | Write the expected ratio as a formula over the config and revisit the side-choice rule. | t7 |

### B1 — the missile fan can't be configured
§2.8 gives the rack `ROCKET_BATTERY` with fan_count 5, spread 40°, salvo 1, pursuit 0 and cooldown 6.0. `TurretMountSlot` only exports variant, rest bearing, turn-rate override, traverse override and pool period factor. `TurretMountScenes` maps the variant to the shared `rocket_battery_mount.tscn`, which authors salvo 2, pursuit 0.333 and cooldown 5.5. `TurretMountBuilder.build()` sizes the pools from `pool_specs()` at build time, so writing fan or salvo after the build leaves the pools too small. The Carrier writes values after the build, but that only works for changes that lengthen the firing period.

### B2 — one shared gate shrinks the broadside
The planned `attack_gate()` has no argument, but the mount calls the same gate for every weapon. With the cap of 2 reached, the gate can't tell that the middle and rear cannons belong to a side volley that already holds a slot. Bind a per-mount callable after the build, and test that the volley stays whole while the missile rack is firing.

### B3 — the torpedo dies to one shot
`EnemyOrdnance._on_hurt(damage)` calls `_health.decrease(damage)`. The default shot deals 50 (`default.tres`), Gatling 14, Spread 25 and Sniper 40. With 3 HP, the planned "2 hits do not defuse, the 3rd does" row can pass only with hand-emitted 1-damage hits, which no player can produce.

### B4 — the test-time target isn't grounded
§2.14 and t1 demand at least 12 s using `tests/README.md` rules 1–3 only. Phase 10's first task already moved the tick-paced files to 16× and found about 18 more clock files no faster. All the Dreadnought tasks depend on t1, so if it misses its target the whole phase stalls.

### M1–M10
Each has file and line evidence in the review file. In short: compute the one-engine expected ratio from the config; acknowledge the Assault return leg; count 6 broadside shells; quiet the ship through the caps; complete the art task's dependencies and give the plume one owner; add incoming-damage and self-hit rows; add the geometry section to the wake and interceptor tasks; make the torpedo's registration concrete; make the flung chunk deal no damage; and consider splitting the weapons task.
